description.narrative: The main objective of the Project is to develop an integrated transport system to support sustainable economic development in Sichuan province. Local roads will complement the expressway in bringing benefits to rural residents. The Project will (i) reduce traffic accidents and vehicle operating costs; (ii) improve access between Chengdu and Kunming, two major growth centers in southwestern PRC; (iii) provide additional transport capacity to accommodate growing traffic; (iv) provide improved access to employment, markets, and social services, and (v) develop capacity of local communications bureaus. The Project has the following components: (i) construction of a 244 km, four-lane access-controlled toll expressway from Ya'an to Lugu, including access roads, interchanges with toll stations, tunnels, bridges, administrative stations, and service areas; (ii) upgrading of 678 km of local roads to improve access to poor remote areas, and roadside stations; (iii) construction of four public transport centers; (iv) procurement of equipment for road maintenance, toll collection, surveillance and communications, tunnel operation facilities, vehicle weigh stations, road safety, and office administration; (v) land acquisition and resettlement; (vi) consulting services for construction supervision, road safety audit, monitoring and evaluation, and capacity building, and (v) developing capacity of local communications bureaus for maintenance. The key inputs needed to implement the Project include civil works, consultants, equipment, and staff of the Sichuan Provincial Transportation Department.

Output: Developing capacity of local communications bureaus for maintenance. Indicator: Develop a 50 person-month training program through the Sichuan Communications and Technology Management College to enhance the local communications bureau staff's capacity and skills in road maintenance and traffic management and thus ensure sustainable operation of the local road component. Progress/Status: The IA with assistance from the international consultant had conducted 50 person-months training through the Sichuan Communications and Technology Management College to enhance the local communications bureau staff's capacity and skills in road maintenance and traffic management. The international consultant had also provided on-site trainings on the subjects including health and safety, project performance management system, benefit monitoring and evaluation, road safety, tunnel construction, geo-technical engineering, bridge engineering, geo-technical engineering, bridge construction, vehicle emission control, and environment protection. During project construction, the IA had conducted numerous on-site trainings for cumulative 5,539 staffs covering subjects as accounting, general office administration, project archiving, application of various advanced construction technology, quality control, safety, environment protection, payment processing, land acquisition and resettlement, and anti-corruption etc. Data Source: Project progress reports, review missions and PCR. Output: Upgrading of 678 km of local roads to improve access to poor remote areas, and roadside stations. Indicator: 678 km of local roads are upgraded in the project area. Progress/Status: The local roads component consists of Part A and B. Part A totaling 158.1 km is financed by ADB and Part B totaling 520.0 km is financed by government. The local roads under Part A were completed upgrading and utilized as access during and for the project expressway construction works. The construction and upgrading of local roads under Part B were implemented through respective county and municipal communications bureaus under the oversight of SPTD. Construction of local roads commenced in 2007 and all works were completed during the second quarter of 2012. Data Source: Project progress reports and PCR. Actual value:
